questions.question: Which correction fixes the spelling in: "check what comsumed so much traffic going through proxy?"
options: A. Check what consumed so much traffic going through the proxy?
B. Check what comsumed so much traffic going through proxy?
C. Check what consumed so much traffic go through proxy?
D. Check what is comsuming so much traffic through the proxy?
questions.explanation: "Consumed" is the correct past participle of "consume." Add "the" before "proxy" for natural phrasing.

questions.question: Which is the best fix for: "Did the TTS deploy on the rockchip board"?
options: A. Did the TTS deploy on the Rockchip board?
B. Was TTS deployed on the Rockchip board?
C. Does TTS deployed on the rockchip board?
D. Has the TTS deploy on the Rockchip board?
questions.explanation: Use passive voice: "Was TTS deployed…" Capitalize "Rockchip" as a proper noun.

questions.question: In "should we refactor it? cause it should provide all middleware servcies", what two fixes are needed?
options: A. Replace "cause" with "because" and "servcies" with "services"
B. Replace "cause" with "cuz" and keep "servcies"
C. Replace "refactor" with "re-factor" and "servcies" with "service"
D. No changes needed; both words are correct
questions.explanation: In formal writing use "because" instead of "cause." "Servcies" is a misspelling of "services."

questions.question: Which correction fixes the spelling in: "search online for RKNN2 convertion tools"?
options: A. Search online for RKNN2 conversion tools.
B. Search online for RKNN2 convertion tools.
C. Search online for RKNN2 converting tools.
D. Search online for RKNN2 convert tools.
questions.explanation: The noun form is "conversion," not "convertion." Capitalize the first word when it starts a sentence.

questions.question: Which correction fixes the error in: "check if they are the write files?"
options: A. Check if they are the right files.
B. Check if they are the write files.
C. Check if they are the wright files.
D. Check if they is the right files.
questions.explanation: "Right" means correct; "write" is a verb meaning to compose text. This was tagged [ERR] in today's log.

questions.question: Why was "perception-service" renamed to "middleware-service" in the edgeAgent project?
options: A. The service only handled computer vision, not audio
B. The name was misleading because the service also provides TTS and other middleware functions
C. Rockchip boards require binaries to be named "middleware"
D. The HTTP server was replaced with a gRPC server
questions.explanation: Today's log notes that "perception-service" was inappropriate because it includes TTS (an action) and should provide broader middleware services.

questions.question: Rewrite as a natural technical question: "Does the board have one Soc or two SoC? Does one SoC have two chips?"
questions.modelAnswer: Does the board have one SoC or two SoCs? Does a single SoC contain two chips?
questions.explanation: Capitalize "SoC" consistently. Use "contain" or "include" for chip layout. Pluralize "SoCs" when referring to two.

questions.question: Rewrite as a clear technical question: "What is crates in rust?"
questions.explanation: "Crates" is plural, so use "are" not "is." Capitalize "Rust" as a proper noun for the programming language.

questions.question: Translate into natural technical English the intent behind: "查一下代理走了多少流量" (in the spirit of today's proxy-traffic debugging).
questions.modelAnswer: Check how much traffic is going through the proxy.
questions.explanation: This matches the debugging context from the log. "Going through the proxy" is the standard phrasing for proxy bandwidth investigation.

questions.question: Rewrite as a professional question: "Is there any risk of breaking anything?"
questions.modelAnswer: Is there any risk of breaking something?
questions.explanation: "Anything" in a negative question often sounds informal. "Breaking something" or "causing any issues" is clearer in a technical review context.
